title: rachel-estrada-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-02
content:
Quick scratchpad for ongoing evals and regression notes. Bare-bones, meant for me + Maya + Sam.

Context:
- Running spot checks on recent Dedicated inference rollout (quantized INT8 builds + kernel swap).
- Goal: capture ad-hoc rubric, representative prompts, and any clear regressions compared to baseline (v2025-11).
- Not exhaustive. Will convert to proper PRD if we have consistent regressions.

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3 scale, per-example; average across sample set):
- 3 = correct & succinct: answer is factually correct, directly addresses prompt, no hallucination, concise.
- 2 = mostly correct: correct but either verbose or misses minor detail; acceptable for UI.
- 1 = flawed: partially correct or misses critical piece; risky for production.
- 0 = incorrect/hallucinated or unsafe.

Evaluation buckets to track (rough):
- Safety/regeneration (hallucination, refuses when should answer)
- Factuality (dates, numbers, entity facts)
- Instruction-following (formatting, list outputs, code fences)
- Conciseness & verbosity (overly long vs terse)
- Latency/partial outputs (streaming artifacts)

Sample prompt set (small, used for quick sanity checks):
1) "Summarize the user research findings from the 2026 Q1 interviews in 3 bullets."
2) "Convert the following to JSON: name: Sam Chen, role: SRE, active: yes"
3) "Explain why transformers use positional encodings in one sentence."
4) "List the tradeoffs of int8 quantization vs fp16 for LLM inference (3 bullets)."
5) "Given: \"The conference is on 2026-04-12 in Seattle.\" Extract date and city."

Representative outputs observed (baseline v2025-11 vs candidate int8-kernel-v2):
--- Prompt 1 ---
Baseline (v2025-11):
1. Consolidated themes: onboarding friction; docs gaps; inconsistent task labels.
2. Users value quick examples and templates.
3. Need for better in-app guidance and onboarding metrics.
Rubric scores: [3,2,3] -> avg 2.67

Candidate (int8-kernel-v2):
1. Onboarding friction and unclear docs.
2. Need for templates and examples.
3. Add in-app messaging and analytics.
Rubric scores: [2,2,2] -> avg 2.0
Notes: content OK but more verbose and repeats phrases; lost "consolidated" phrasing. Slightly lower precision.

--- Prompt 2 ---
Baseline: {"name":"Sam Chen","role":"SRE","active":true}
Candidate: {"name": "Sam Chen", "role": "SRE", "active": "yes"}
Rubric: baseline 3, candidate 1 (type changed).
Observation: candidate preserves text but fails to normalize booleans -> regression flagged.

--- Prompt 3 ---
Baseline: "Transformers use positional encodings to give the model information about token order, since attention is permutation-invariant." (3)
Candidate: "Positional encodings let the model know positions of tokens so it can learn order relationships." (3)
Notes: equivalent. No regression.

--- Prompt 4 ---
Baseline: "1) Reduced memory and compute, 2) potential slight accuracy loss, 3) faster throughput on CPUs/GPUs with optimized kernels." (2)
Candidate: "1) Smaller model footprint, 2) accuracy can drop, 3) often faster but may need calibration." (2)
Notes: both acceptable; candidate uses cautionary phrasing.

--- Prompt 5 ---
Baseline: {"date":"2026-04-12","city":"Seattle"} (3)
Candidate: {"date":"2026-04-12","city":"Seattle"} (3)

Summary of regressions so far:
- Strongest regression: boolean normalization broken in candidate build (prompt 2). Likely stringification in post-processing step after quantized infer (PR #412?).
- Slight drop in conciseness/precision in free-text summarization (prompt 1). Candidate repeats phrases and reduces crispness. Could be kernel reorder or temperature default shift.
- No major safety regressions observed in this small set.

Quick root-cause hypotheses / triage steps:
1) Post-processing changes: check serialization code path for categorical/boolean normalization (compare commit diffs in PR 412).
2) Tokenization/decoder behavior: verify top-k/top-p defaults and temperature between baseline and candidate; also check any float->int rounding artifacts.
3) Quantization calibration: run calibration validation set related to numeric/boolean outputs. Might need label-preserving calibration for classification-like behaviors.

Immediate action items (TODO):
- [ ] Reproduce boolean bug locally with minimal script (Sam) -> link test case to JIRA EVAL-293.
- [ ] Run a larger prompt sweep (~200 examples across buckets) and compute avg rubric scores (Rachel/Maya).
- [ ] Check model config defaults in deployment (temp/p/p) and add explicit overrides in candidate config if mismatched.
- [ ] Add unit test for JSON normalization (booleans/ints) in post-process pipeline.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is this regression specific to certain sequence lengths? Need to log token counts for failing examples.
- Does streaming vs non-streaming change the post-processing path? Candidate was tested both ways; double-check artifacts.
- If quantization is the culprit, do we revert kernel swap or tune calibration first? Tradeoff: reverting costs performance.

Scratch: quick command to run local sweep (for devs):
python tools/eval_sweep.py --model candidate-int8-kernel-v2 --prompts tests/eval_prompts/sanity_small.json --write outputs/candidate_sanity.json

Notes for PR/hand-off:
- Include a couple of failing examples (prompt 2) in the PR description to make triage easier.
- Link to Confluence prompt set page (see linked artifacts) and update after sweep.

End of scratchpad. Will flesh into proper report if counts show regressions >0.2 avg score drop across rubric.
